extraction_metadata.source_type: LinkedIn post (European Radiology opinion paper share)
extraction_metadata.notes: ESR Journals (European Society of Radiology) sharing an opinion paper from European Radiology on post-deployment monitoring of foundation models in radiology. Comment thread includes practising radiologists (Amit Gupta MD, Vera Sorin) converging on institutional observability. This is the strongest OSIRIS-aligned signal this round: the paper argues monitoring final outputs is insufficient — you must monitor the entire system pathway.

title: Post-deployment monitoring of foundation models in radiology: outputs aren't enough
subtitle_or_tagline: European Radiology opinion paper — behavioural drift must be detected at the system-pathway level, not the output level
topic: An opinion paper in European Radiology (Sorin, Wald, Klang, Korfiatis, Collins; ACR-affiliated) arguing that post-deployment monitoring of foundation models in radiology must go far beyond checking final outputs, because model behaviour is shaped by invisible deployment settings, user prompts, and dynamic retrieval contexts. The authors call for institutional deployment with true observability so health systems can detect behavioural drift before it affects patient care. The opening anecdote — a resident relying on an unmonitored personal chatbot at 4 a.m. — frames the governance stakes.

workflow_steps: Step 1 - Deploy foundation model under institutional (not personal) management
Step 2 - Instrument the full inference pathway: prompts, retrieval contexts, model versions
Step 3 - Monitor for behavioural drift across settings, not just output accuracy
Step 4 - Alert before drift affects patient care
Step 5 - Feed governance learnings back into deployment policy
key_claims: Post-deployment monitoring must go beyond checking final outputs
Model behaviour is shaped by invisible deployment settings, user prompts, and dynamic retrieval contexts
Institutional deployment with true observability is a prerequisite for safe clinical infrastructure
Health systems must detect behavioural drift before it affects patient care
caveats_or_warnings: Opinion paper — proposes a governance framework rather than reporting a validated monitoring system
Implementation cost of full-pathway observability at health-system scale is not quantified
citations: Sorin V, Wald C, Klang E, Korfiatis P, Collins J. Post-deployment monitoring of foundation models in radiology: Why outputs aren't enough. European Radiology (2026)

osiris_connection: This paper is the clinical-governance version of the OSIRIS thesis. 'Behavioural drift' is precisely what Theorem 7 bounds: every model update, prompt shift, or retrieval-context change is a displacement, and cumulative displacement needs a bound (sum of L*c across the update path). The paper's demand for 'true observability' of the full pathway is operationally equivalent to OSIRIS's per-update (L, c) audit trail — the platform's extraction graph is exactly the artifact such an observability regime would produce. Where the paper says 'monitor the pathway, not the outputs', OSIRIS says 'certify each displacement, so the pathway's total drift is bounded by construction'.
